newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM blasts anti-Burma protesters.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM blasts anti-Burma protesters.

text.p: First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Thursday accused Cambodians who demonstrated against a visit by Burma's military leader of betraying their country's tradition of hospitality.

"I feel very sorry that some Khmers have 'de-Khmerised.' They are not any more Khmers, because if you are Khmer, you have to abide by our traditions," said the prince, speaking at a United Nations conference on poverty.
"The tradition of Asian people is...to very warmly welcome and to provide hospitality to the guests of the nation, the guests of King (Norodom Sihanouk)," he said.

One hour before the arrival of Burmese General Than Shwe on Wednesday, opposition leader Sam Rainsy led several dozen protesters from his Khmer Nation Party (KNP) on a march through the capital, defying government orders not to hold the demonstration.
Hundreds of police pursued the protesters through the streets in a vain attempt to stop the hour-long demonstration in support of Burmese democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi.

Burma's State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) recently barred opposition leader Suu Kyi from giving regular weekly speeches at her home, and last month the SLORC arrested hundreds of her party's activists, releasing them in stages.

Prince Ranariddh declined to comment on the demonstration on Wednesday, saying he wanted to wait until Than Shwe had departed. But he said on Thursday at the close of a speech on poverty that he felt compelled to speak out against the protest.

"I beg your pardon, but as prime minister of Cambodia, I have to spell out this principle very clearly," he said. "We have to be very strict and very respectful to one principle -- not to interfere in the internal affairs of any country."
Prince Ranariddh accused Sam Rainsy of returning from Paris, where he keeps a second home, to make trouble rather than to help his nation.
Prince Ranariddh and co-Premier Hun Sen met Than Shwe on Thursday morning. Than Shwe's four-day visit is his first to Cambodia since diplomatic ties were restored in 1994, officials said.
